subject: docs: developer-guide recovery section describes in-process reinit that doesn't exist
content:
## Problem

The Recovery section of developer-guide.md describes three behaviors that do
not exist in agent/src/main.c. All three are doc inaccuracies — the code is
correct, the docs are wrong.

## Discrepancies

**1. "No lighthouses at start" row:**
> Agent automatically reinitializes libsurvive every 60 seconds until poses arrive.

Actual behavior: agent exits (breaks from main loop) after 60s with no tracker
object found. systemd restarts the service. There is no in-process reinit loop.

**2. "libsurvive shutdown" row:**
> Agent attempts reinit immediately, retrying every 10 seconds.

Actual behavior: agent exits when `tracker_is_running()` returns false. Again,
systemd handles the retry. There is no in-process reinit or 10s retry counter.

**3. "SHTC REINIT" command description:**
> rate-limited to once per 10 seconds

No rate limiting exists in the agent. The REINIT command causes an immediate
exit (sets g_running = 0). If this rate limit exists, it is enforced by the
Windows client, not the agent.

## Suggested fix

Update the two table rows to say "agent exits (code 0); systemd restarts
automatically" rather than implying in-process reinit. Add a note to the SHTC
REINIT entry clarifying that rate limiting is enforced by the client.

Found during recovery state machine refactor.

subject: agent: tracker_lost_logged never resets after tracking recovers
content:
## Bug

`tracker_lost_logged` is reset to `false` only inside the `if (!announced)`
branch in `main.c` — which fires exactly once, on first-ever tracking acquisition.

If tracking is subsequently lost (30s no poses) and recovers before the 300s
restart threshold, `tracker_lost_logged` is never cleared. The "no pose updates
for 30s" warning will not fire for any subsequent dropout in the same agent
lifetime.

**Observed:** at-most-one warning per agent lifetime.
**Expected:** at-most-one warning per dropout episode.

## Location

agent/src/main.c — reset only happens inside `if (!announced)`, which is never
true after first acquisition:

    if (tracker_get_pose(tracker, &pose)) {
        if (!announced) {     // <-- only fires once ever
            announced = true;
            tracker_lost_logged = false;
        }
    }

## Fix (not applied — found during recovery state machine refactor)

Reset `tracker_lost_logged = false` whenever a pose is received while
`announced` is already true and `tracker_lost_logged` is true — i.e. on
recovery from POSE_LOST, not only on first-ever acquisition.

subject: GSS re-solve: MP_MAXITER result accepted by --max-cal-error, corrupts calibration
content:
## Summary

When the Watchman radio scan causes a brief USB dropout, libsurvive triggers a
GSS re-solve on resumption. If that re-solve hits the iteration limit (MP_MAXITER)
without converging, it still passes the `--max-cal-error 0.01` gate because
`sensor_err` appears just under the threshold — even though the result is
meaningless. The corrupt calibration is written to config.json, causing a boot
loop on the next agent restart.

## Observed values (real log)

| Metric | Good solve | Bad solve (MP_MAXITER) |
|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| Stop reason | MP_OK_BOTH | MP_MAXITER (hit 200 iter limit) |
| sensor_err | 0.000124 rad | 0.008954 rad ← passes our gate |
| bestnorm | 58.5 | 863,358.7 (15,000× worse) |
| Accepted? | ✅ | ✅ should be ❌ |

## Root cause

`--max-cal-error` is a libsurvive flag that gates on `sensor_err < threshold`.
It does not check the MPFIT convergence status. A solve that returns MP_MAXITER
did not converge — the reported sensor_err is the residual at the iteration
limit, not a meaningful calibration quality metric.

## Trigger sequence

1. Watchman radio scan → USB timeout on IMU (ep 0x81) and Lightcap (ep 0x83) simultaneously (~2s)
2. USB resumes → libsurvive GSS re-solves with all 3 lighthouses
3. Re-solve returns MP_MAXITER, sensor_err=0.008954 (just under 0.01)
4. Bad calibration written to ~/.config/libsurvive/config.json
5. Agent exits; restarts load corrupt config → no poses → SIGABRT boot loop

## Fix

In the GSS result callback in agent/src/tracker.c, check the MPFIT convergence
status before accepting a result. Reject any solve that returns MP_MAXITER,
MP_BADSTEP, or other non-OK codes regardless of sensor_err.

Also log the stop reason string alongside sensor_err and bestnorm so this is
visible in journalctl without decoding the libsurvive INFO line.

## Workaround

Delete ~/.config/libsurvive/config.json to force fresh calibration on restart:

    ssh stagehand@<pi-ip> "rm -f ~/.config/libsurvive/config.json && sudo systemctl restart stagehand-agent"
